title: Parables Series Roadmap
status: Approved by Jamie Dennis on November 1 2026

weeks.summary: Begin with why Jesus used parables, then let his explanation of the Sower establish how we will listen throughout the series.
weeks.question: What is helping or hindering me as I receive Jesus' words?
weeks.context: Day 1 introduces the series. Days 2 through 6 follow the Sower's distinct responses to the word. Day 7 connects hearing with putting Jesus' teaching into practice.

days.title: Why Jesus Told Stories
days.focus: Jesus' parables disclose the kingdom while confronting resistant hearing; understanding calls for receptive hearts.

days.title: A Sower Went Out
days.focus: The same seed meets different ground. Introduce the whole story before exploring Jesus' explanation.

days.title: When the Word Stays on the Surface
days.focus: Jesus connects the path with hearing without understanding and the wicked one's removal of the word.

days.title: Roots for the Difficult Days
days.focus: An eager beginning needs depth when trouble or persecution comes because of the word.

days.title: What Is Crowding the Word
days.focus: Life's cares and the deceitfulness of riches can crowd out the word and its fruit.

days.title: A Heart That Bears Fruit
days.focus: Hearing with understanding bears fruit; Jesus describes differing yields within a fruitful response.

days.title: The Foundation Beneath the House
days.focus: Jesus connects a secure foundation with hearing his sayings and doing them.

weeks.summary: Explore the kingdom's growth and incomparable worth through seed, leaven, treasure, and a pearl.
weeks.question: How is Jesus reshaping what I consider significant and valuable?
weeks.context: Keep growth and value centered on God's kingdom. The growing seed, mustard seed, and leaven use different pictures of its working; treasure and pearl emphasize its worth.

days.title: Growing While We Sleep
days.focus: The seed grows beyond the farmer's understanding, inviting trust in God's work beyond human control.

days.title: The Harvest Will Come
days.focus: The story moves through growth to harvest, giving the kingdom's quiet beginning a purposeful destination.

days.title: A Beginning Easy to Overlook
days.focus: A small beginning can conceal the scale of the kingdom Jesus is announcing.

days.title: Branches Beyond the Beginning
days.focus: The seed's mature growth reveals a reach far greater than its initial appearance suggests.

days.title: Until the Whole Was Leavened
days.focus: Leaven's unseen, pervasive action pictures the kingdom's far-reaching effect.

days.title: The Joy of Finding Treasure
days.focus: The kingdom's surpassing worth explains the finder's joyful, wholehearted response.

days.title: The Pearl Worth Everything
days.focus: Recognizing the kingdom's value reorders the merchant's priorities and possessions.

weeks.summary: Read Luke 15 as Jesus' response to criticism of his welcome, tracing the joy of recovery through three stories.
weeks.question: Where do I recognize myself in these stories of being lost, welcomed, and invited to rejoice?
weeks.context: Luke 15:1-2 supplies the setting. The father goes out to both sons. The older brother's unresolved response leaves Jesus' hearers facing their own response to mercy.

days.title: The Shepherd Goes After the One
days.focus: Jesus answers criticism of his welcome with a shepherd who actively seeks the lost sheep.

days.title: Heaven's Joy Over One
days.focus: Jesus explicitly connects the shepherd's celebration with heaven's joy over a sinner who repents.

days.title: The Search and the Celebration
days.focus: Diligent searching ends in shared joy; Jesus again highlights rejoicing over repentance.

days.title: The Road Into the Far Country
days.focus: The younger son's departure and loss expose the ruin of life separated from his father.

days.title: Coming to Himself
days.focus: The son's awakening becomes confession and a return to the father he has wronged.

days.title: The Father Runs to Meet Him
days.focus: The father's compassion and welcome illuminate the mercy celebrated throughout the chapter.

days.title: The Brother Outside the Celebration
days.focus: The older son's resentment challenges hearers to examine their response to another person's welcome.

weeks.summary: Move from receiving mercy to forgiveness, grateful love, and the challenge of celebrating another person's generosity.
weeks.question: What happens in my heart when mercy reaches someone whose story differs from mine?
weeks.context: Keep Peter's forgiveness question with the unforgiving servant, and keep Simon's dinner with the two debtors. The laborers confront comparison through the landowner's generosity.

days.title: How Many Times Must I Forgive
days.focus: Peter's question introduces forgiveness that cannot be reduced to keeping a tally.

days.title: The Debt He Could Never Repay
days.focus: The king's compassion cancels an overwhelming debt the servant cannot repay.

days.title: Mercy at the Next Door
days.focus: Refusing a fellow servant mercy exposes a grave contradiction in receiving forgiveness.

days.title: Two Debtors and One Creditor
days.focus: Both debtors lack the means to pay; cancellation frames Jesus' question about love.

days.title: When Forgiveness Becomes Love
days.focus: Jesus connects the woman's grateful love, forgiveness, and faith within Simon's judgmental response.

days.title: The Generous Landowner
days.focus: The landowner's generosity challenges expectations that the kingdom operates by comparative entitlement.

days.title: When Generosity Feels Unfair
days.focus: The first workers' resentment invites examination of envy toward generosity shown to others.

weeks.summary: Explore mercy across boundaries, the invitation to God's banquet, and humility at the table.
weeks.question: Whom might I see differently after listening to Jesus?
weeks.context: The lawyer seeks to justify himself before asking about his neighbor. Luke 14 places banquet teaching among questions of status, hospitality, and who belongs at the table.

days.title: Who Is My Neighbor
days.focus: Jesus answers the lawyer's boundary-setting question through the mercy shown by an unexpected neighbor.

days.title: The Compassion That Crossed the Road
days.focus: The Samaritan's compassion becomes practical care involving time, resources, and personal involvement.

days.title: Becoming a Neighbor
days.focus: Jesus turns attention toward the person who shows mercy and calls his hearer to respond.

days.title: An Invitation Interrupted by Excuses
days.focus: Ordinary commitments become excuses for declining the host's invitation.

days.title: A Table for the Overlooked
days.focus: The host welcomes people excluded from expected circles of honor and access.

days.title: The Invitation Calls for an Answer
days.focus: A generous invitation carries urgency; those who refuse it miss the feast.

days.title: Taking the Lower Place
days.focus: Jesus confronts the pursuit of status and teaches humility before the one who gives honor.

weeks.summary: Bring need, weariness, self-righteousness, and service before God through Jesus' teaching on prayer and humility.
weeks.question: What am I bringing to God honestly, and what am I still trying to prove?
weeks.context: Read the midnight friend with Jesus' teaching on the Father's goodness. Read the unjust judge as a contrast that strengthens confidence in God's justice. Luke names self-righteousness as the next parable's target.

days.title: A Knock in the Middle of the Night
days.focus: A request made in need introduces bold, persistent asking in Jesus' teaching on prayer.

days.title: The Father Who Gives Good Gifts
days.focus: Jesus grounds asking in the heavenly Father's goodness and his gift of the Holy Spirit.

days.title: Praying When Weariness Sets In
days.focus: Luke states the purpose: keep praying and resist losing heart.

days.title: Will He Find Faith
days.focus: Jesus directs confidence toward God's justice and closes with a searching question about enduring faith.

days.title: The Prayer That Compares
days.focus: The Pharisee's comparison exposes self-trust and contempt for others in the setting of prayer.

days.title: The Prayer That Asks for Mercy
days.focus: The publican depends on God's mercy, and Jesus declares that he goes home justified.

days.title: Serving Without Keeping an Account
days.focus: Faithful obedience calls for humility; service gives us no claim of entitlement over God.

weeks.summary: Consider possessions, foresight, divided allegiance, and the cost of following Jesus.
weeks.question: What do my plans and possessions reveal about where I am seeking security?
weeks.context: Read the steward through Jesus' following instructions on faithfulness and serving God. The tower and king belong to his explicit teaching on the cost of discipleship.

days.title: Bigger Barns and a Smaller Horizon
days.focus: The farmer's abundance exposes a life defined by possessions and plans centered on himself.

days.title: The Night He Had Not Planned For
days.focus: The sudden demand for his life reveals how little stored wealth can secure.

days.title: Being Rich Toward God
days.focus: Jesus' conclusion redirects the question from accumulated goods to one's relationship with God.

days.title: A Steward Who Saw What Was Coming
days.focus: The steward's urgent foresight introduces Jesus' challenge to use present resources with eternity in view.

days.title: The Master My Money Serves
days.focus: Jesus connects faithful stewardship with undivided allegiance to God.

days.title: Before You Build the Tower
days.focus: The unfinished tower makes the cost of following Jesus a matter for serious consideration.

days.title: The King Who Had to Reckon
days.focus: The king's reckoning reinforces the need to face the surrender involved in discipleship.

weeks.summary: Follow Jesus' confrontation of empty agreement and resistant leadership, then consider the urgency of repentance.
weeks.question: Where is Jesus inviting an honest response beyond words of agreement?
weeks.context: Matthew 21 identifies the leaders who recognize themselves in Jesus' stories. The tenants point toward rejection of the Son and the rejected cornerstone. Luke 13 frames the fig tree with a call to repentance.

days.title: The Son Who Changed His Mind
days.focus: A refusal followed by repentance and action challenges assumptions about who responds to God.

days.title: The Yes That Never Became a Step
days.focus: Respectful words without obedience expose the distance between profession and response.

days.title: A Vineyard Held in Trust
days.focus: The tenants treat entrusted property as their own and resist the owner's rightful claim.

days.title: They Rejected the Son
days.focus: The tenants' violence toward the son anticipates the rejection Jesus is confronting.

days.title: The Stone the Builders Rejected
days.focus: Jesus links rejection with God's purpose through the Scripture about the cornerstone.

days.title: Another Season of Mercy
days.focus: The gardener's plea pictures patient opportunity within Jesus' urgent call to repentance.

days.title: The Fruit God Is Seeking
days.focus: The tree's continued care carries an expectation of fruit and a real limit to delay.

weeks.summary: Hold patience, judgment, and hope together while listening to Jesus' own explanation of the wheat and tares.
weeks.question: How can I entrust final judgment to God while taking Jesus' words seriously today?
weeks.context: Jesus identifies the field as the world and the harvest as the end of the age. Day 63 is a reflection across Matthew 13, bringing its several kingdom images together.

days.title: When Tares Appear in the Field
days.focus: The appearance of destructive growth raises the servants' question about the owner's good seed.

days.title: Let Both Grow Until the Harvest
days.focus: The owner restrains premature uprooting; Jesus identifies the world and the final harvest.

days.title: The Righteous Will Shine
days.focus: Jesus' explanation joins the reality of judgment with hope for the righteous in the Father's kingdom.

days.title: The Net Gathered Every Kind
days.focus: The net's broad gathering leads toward a final separation in Jesus' kingdom comparison.

days.title: When the Catch Reaches Shore
days.focus: Jesus explicitly connects the sorting with final judgment, giving the present invitation weight.

days.title: Treasures New and Old
days.focus: Understanding the kingdom equips a teacher to bring forth treasures new and old.

days.title: Hearing the Kingdom Across the Stories
days.focus: Bring growth, worth, judgment, and understanding together as a response to Jesus' kingdom teaching.

weeks.summary: Explore waiting as faithful readiness, responsibility toward others, and a personal response to the coming Lord.
weeks.question: What would readiness for Jesus look like in the life I am living today?
weeks.context: Luke's waiting servants receive a surprising picture of the master's welcome. All ten virgins become sleepy; the distinction concerns preparation for the bridegroom's arrival. Keep the focus on Jesus' call to readiness.

days.title: Lamps Burning While We Wait
days.focus: Jesus calls his servants to live ready for a return whose timing they cannot control.

days.title: The Master Who Serves His Servants
days.focus: The master's unexpected service pictures the gracious welcome promised to watchful servants.

days.title: Faithful in the Master's Household
days.focus: The wise steward fulfills entrusted responsibility by caring for the household while the master is away.

days.title: When Delay Becomes an Excuse
days.focus: Assuming a delayed return becomes a pretext for abuse, exposing accountability for entrusted responsibility.

days.title: Waiting for the Bridegroom
days.focus: The whole wedding party waits through delay, but preparation distinguishes the wise from the foolish.

days.title: Readiness Cannot Be Borrowed
days.focus: At the bridegroom's arrival, another person's preparation cannot supply one's own lack.

days.title: The Door and the Invitation Today
days.focus: The closed door gives urgency to Jesus' command to watch for his coming.

weeks.summary: Read the talents and pounds in their distinct settings, considering faithful service, fear, accountability, and watchfulness.
weeks.question: What has been entrusted to me, and how am I responding to the one who entrusted it?
weeks.context: Talents and pounds are money within these stories. Their teaching concerns faithful responsibility and accountability. Luke 19:11 explains the pounds' setting: expectations that the kingdom would appear immediately.

days.title: What the Master Placed in Their Hands
days.focus: The master entrusts differing amounts, establishing responsibility in relationship to what each servant receives.

days.title: Faithfulness and the Master's Joy
days.focus: The first two servants receive the same commendation for faithful use of what was entrusted.

days.title: When Fear Buries What Was Given
days.focus: The last servant's account of his master and his fear accompany a refusal to act.

days.title: The Kingdom and the Time Between
days.focus: Jesus addresses expectations of an immediate kingdom through a nobleman's departure and promised return.

days.title: Doing Business Until He Returns
days.focus: The servants' entrusted work gives substance to faithfulness during their lord's absence.

days.title: An Account Before the Returning King
days.focus: The king's return brings accountability for neglected trust and rejection of his rule.

days.title: Each Servant Has Work to Do
days.focus: Jesus connects assigned work with watchfulness while the time of the master's return remains unknown.

weeks.summary: Return to the invitation itself, exploring response to the King's Son, Jesus' presence, and resistance to God's messengers.
weeks.question: Where might familiarity, distraction, or criticism be keeping me from receiving Jesus?
weeks.context: The wedding garment has differing interpretations; the devotional should identify its clear emphasis on an appropriate response to the king. Read cloth and wineskins within the question about fasting and the bridegroom.

days.title: The King Prepared a Feast
days.focus: The king's invitation for his son's wedding meets indifference and violent rejection.

days.title: Guests From the Highways
days.focus: The invitation reaches beyond the first guests and gathers people from the roads.

days.title: A Response Worthy of the Invitation
days.focus: The wedding garment scene gives weight to the response required by the king's invitation.

days.title: Joy in the Bridegroom's Presence
days.focus: Jesus explains his disciples' present joy and coming fasting through the bridegroom's presence and departure.

days.title: Making Room for What Jesus Brings
days.focus: The paired images illuminate Jesus' new work and the resistance created by attachment to the familiar.

days.title: When Every Messenger Is Criticized
days.focus: Jesus exposes a generation's refusal of both John's austerity and his own table fellowship.

days.title: Recognizing Wisdom by Its Fruit
days.focus: Jesus' conclusion invites recognition of God's wisdom through its outworking amid hostile judgments.

weeks.summary: Close with six deliberate reflection days, revisiting earlier passages and leaving room for prayer and personal response.
weeks.question: What do I want to keep bringing before God after this series ends?
weeks.context: These six entries are revisits, each with a fresh reflective question. They return the reader to Jesus' words and their own relationship with God as the series closes.

days.title: What Am I Building On
days.focus: Revisit the foundation: where are Jesus' words becoming part of the way I live?

days.title: The Mercy I Have Received
days.focus: Revisit forgiveness: how is the mercy I have received shaping my response to others?

days.title: Whom Am I Passing By
days.focus: Revisit neighbor-love: whose need am I beginning to see differently?

days.title: What Is Worth Everything
days.focus: Revisit the kingdom's worth: what is Jesus changing about my priorities?

days.title: What Has Been Placed in My Care
days.focus: Revisit entrusted responsibility: what needs an honest response to God today?

days.title: How Am I Hearing Jesus Now
days.focus: Return to the opening story: what has taken root, and what do I want to bring before God?
